comment: Written by src/app/api/mcp/workspace-eval.fixture.spec.ts from the real catalog; served by scripts/turn_census/fixture_workspace.py. Regenerate with UPDATE_FIXTURES=1.

operations.name: project-cleanup-confirm
operations.summary: Move the chosen documents to the Papierkorb
operations.description: Puts the documents the person chose (`documentIds`) into the Papierkorb, all or nothing; they can be restored for 14 days. `proposedIds` is what project-cleanup-propose suggested and `aiUsed` says whether a proposal was used. Never send ids the person did not approve.

operations.name: project-cleanup-propose
operations.summary: Have Piloti propose what to clear out
operations.description: Before a project closes („Ausmisten"): Piloti proposes which documents the finished project no longer needs, among those the person may read and write. Starts a paid model call, so call it once. Nothing is removed. Show the proposal to the person, then send their choice with project-cleanup-confirm.

operations.name: project-consistency-check
operations.description: Asks the backend model whether the intake’s free-text answers contradict the structured answers (passed as context). Best effort: always answers `{ findings, error? }`, and an error means proceed. Call before saving a profile edited in free text.

operations.name: project-create
operations.description: Creates a project in the organization and returns it with its id. Give a name; optionally the address (a geocoder hit as `location`, or typed `address`), a description, and `setup`: `piloti` (default) has Piloti read the documents afterwards, `self` leaves the profile to the intake wizard. To add a past project as a reference, pass `closing` with the outcome and months. Call project-same-address-list first to avoid a duplicate. Next: upload documents, then project-intake-get to follow the reading.

operations.name: project-delete
operations.summary: Move a project to the recently deleted list
operations.description: Soft-deletes a project; it is purged after the date the response names and can be restored until then (project-restore). Requires `confirmName`, the project’s exact current name, as the dialog does.

operations.name: project-experience-extract
operations.summary: Extract experience from a closing project
operations.description: Reads the project’s own documents once and stores what they say as suggestions: unconfirmed facts on the project profile and drafted decisions in project memory, which a person then confirms or dismisses. Refused for a closed project. Starts a paid model call. Needs project:memory:write or project:edit.

operations.name: project-get
operations.description: One project by id: name, status, dates and the person’s access to it.

operations.name: project-intake-complete
operations.description: Ends the review of the intake. For a past project created with a closing intent this also closes the project with its outcome and Abschluss. Call once project-intake-get shows nothing left to decide. Answers `{ intake }`.

operations.name: project-intake-decide
operations.description: Applies decisions on what Piloti read: `confirm` writes a suggestion (or the alternative at `alternativeIndex`), `dismiss` removes it, `answer` writes the person’s own value, `unknown` records the key as not known. Keys come from project-intake-get. Answers one result per decision, in order, and the intake after them.

operations.name: project-intake-definition-get
operations.description: The static intake questionnaire: the sections and questions, with the keys that project-intake-decide and project-profile-patch use. Read it to learn which key an answer belongs to.

operations.name: project-intake-get
operations.description: The Projekterfassung as the person sees it: what Piloti read from the documents, the suggestions waiting for a decision, reading progress and what is still open. Answers `{ intake }`. Decide on suggestions with project-intake-decide; finish with project-intake-complete.

operations.name: project-intake-start
operations.description: Starts a reading of the project’s documents now. `scope: "new"` reads what is not read yet; `"all"` forgets what was read and starts over. While one reading runs the next is queued. Needs project:memory:write or project:edit and fails with 409 on a closed project. Answers `{ intake }`; poll project-intake-get.

operations.name: project-list
operations.summary: List the projects the person can see
operations.description: Every project the person may open in this organization, with its id, name and lifecycle status. Start here: most other operations take a project id from this list.

operations.name: project-member-add
operations.summary: Give someone a role on a project
operations.description: Assigns a project role (`project-viewer`, `project-contributor`, `project-editor`, `project-admin`) to an organization member, or an empty `roleSlug` to clear their project role. `organizationMembershipId` comes from organization-member-list, not a user id. Needs project:members:manage. Check the result with project-member-list.

operations.name: project-member-list
operations.description: The project roster: each member with their role and the role assignment id (members[].id), plus `viewerUserId`, the caller’s own user id. Needs project:members:manage. Use the assignment id with project-member-remove.

operations.name: project-member-remove
operations.description: Removes one role assignment from a project, so the person loses that access. `assignmentId` is members[].id from project-member-list. Needs project:members:manage. Re-adding is project-member-add.

operations.name: project-memory-create
operations.description: Writes one memory item by hand: a `kind`, the `content` (up to 2000 characters), and optionally `confidence` and `pinned`. Answers `{ item }` with its id. Needs project:memory:write. Check project-memory-list first so you do not repeat an item.

operations.name: project-memory-delete
operations.description: Removes one memory item for good; it cannot be undone. Prefer project-memory-update with status `dismissed` when the item may matter later. `itemId` is from project-memory-list.

operations.name: project-memory-list
operations.description: The facts, decisions and notes Piloti keeps for the project, as `{ items }` with their ids, kind, status, confidence and pinned flag. Pass `includeArchived: "true"` to include archived ones, or `conversationId` for those noted in one conversation. Item ids feed project-memory-update and project-memory-delete.

operations.name: project-memory-update
operations.description: Changes any of a memory item’s kind, content, status, confidence, verification or pinned flag; at least one field. Set `status` to `dismissed` or `superseded` rather than deleting when the item was only wrong for now. `itemId` is from project-memory-list. Answers `{ item }`.

operations.name: project-overview-get
operations.description: The project’s overview as its home page shows it: profile summary, counts and the latest activity. A good first read once you have a project id from project-list.

operations.name: project-period-set
operations.description: Sets the project’s start month (`startedOn`, YYYY-MM, or null to clear). The end is not set here: closing the project names it (project-status-set). Answers the updated Steckbrief.

operations.name: project-person-add
operations.summary: Add a person to the Steckbrief
operations.description: Adds someone to the project’s Steckbrief by hand, such as an external planner: name, optional Funktion, Firma, start and end month. No e-mail or phone is kept. Pass `userId` (an organization member’s user id from organization-member-list) to describe a member instead. Send all fields; use null for unknown.

operations.name: project-person-delete
operations.summary: Erase a person from the Steckbrief
operations.description: Erases one person’s entry from the Steckbrief; this is the data-protection erasure and cannot be undone. Still possible in a closed project for whoever manages it. `personId` is from project-record-get.

operations.name: project-person-update
operations.summary: Change a person on the Steckbrief
operations.description: Replaces one person’s entry with the body given, so send every field (name, function, company, startedOn, endedOn, userId), not only the changed one. `personId` is from project-record-get.

operations.name: project-profile-get
operations.description: The structured project profile (facts, goals, unknowns, assumptions) with its `profileVersion`. Read it before project-profile-patch or project-profile-replace. The profile has one form, the intake wizard; this is its stored result.

operations.name: project-profile-patch
operations.description: Applies JSON-patch style operations (`add`, `replace`, `remove`) to the profile under /facts, /goals, /unknowns or /assumptions. The safer way to edit one fact. Pass `conversationId` when the change came out of a chat. Needs project:edit. Answers the updated profile; read project-profile-get for paths.

operations.name: project-profile-replace
operations.description: Saves the entire profile from project-profile-get, edited. It overwrites everything, so prefer project-profile-patch for a single change. Needs project:edit. The If-Match version header is not sent through this tool, so the route checks the version inside the profile body instead; a 409 means someone saved meanwhile: read again.

operations.name: project-record-get
operations.description: The project’s Steckbrief: its period (Beginn, Abschluss) and the people on it, members and former members included, with their Funktion, Firma and months. people[].id feeds project-person-update and project-person-delete.

operations.name: project-reindex
operations.description: Queues a job that rebuilds the search chunks of every document in the project, and answers 202 with the job id at once. Use when answers seem to miss documents that are on the shelf. It carries on after the call returns and is safe to repeat.

operations.name: project-rename
operations.description: Give a project a new name. Needs the project:manage permission on that project.

operations.name: project-restore
operations.description: Brings a soft-deleted project back during its grace period (see project-delete for the purge date). Needs project:manage. Answers `{ status: "restored" }`.

operations.name: project-same-address-list
operations.description: Up to three projects the person may open that sit at the given address, as `{ projects: [{ id, name, status }] }`. Call before project-create to warn about a duplicate. `label` is the address text; `lat` and `lon` sharpen the match.

operations.name: project-status-set
operations.summary: Pause, resume or close a project
operations.description: Moves a project through its lifecycle. `{ status: "active" }` resumes or reopens, `{ status: "paused" }` pauses, `{ status: "closed", outcome, endedOn }` closes it with how it ended and its Abschluss month (YYYY-MM). Needs project:manage and works on a closed project too. Answers the new status and dates. Before closing, consider project-cleanup-propose.

operations.name: project-summary-generate
operations.description: Generates the profile summary with the backend model and stores it on the profile, replacing the earlier one. Needs project:edit. Answers the summary. Optionally pass `locale` ("de" or "en").

operations.name: project-upload-screening-get
operations.description: The upload screening policy in force for this project: the office’s list and what the project adds to or removes from its name terms. Any member may read it. Edit with project-upload-screening-set.

operations.name: project-upload-screening-set
operations.summary: Set the project’s sensitive name terms
operations.description: Saves the project’s whole override of the sensitive name terms: `addedNameTerms` and `removedNameTerms`. It replaces the earlier override, so read project-upload-screening-get first. Content terms and detectors stay the office’s. Needs project:manage; audited.

operations.name: deletion-list
operations.description: The organization's pending and failed deletions behind the Recently deleted view; failed rows are purges that got stuck. Needs the compliance permission.

operations.name: document-archive
operations.description: Takes a document out of the working set: it leaves the default listings and stops answering questions, but the file and every version stay. Send an empty body. Needs write access on the document’s project.

operations.name: document-by-name-resolve
operations.summary: Find a project’s documents by file name
operations.description: Resolves exact file names to the project’s listing rows (`projectId` from project-list, up to the server’s name limit). Use it when you know the file name but not the id. Read-only.

operations.name: document-delete
operations.description: Erases a project document, its versions and its indexed text. This cannot be undone, and a legal hold refuses it with a 409. To only take a document out of the working set, call document-archive instead.

operations.name: document-download
operations.summary: Get a time-limited download link for a document
operations.description: Mints a presigned URL for the document’s current file and answers `{ downloadUrl, filename, contentType, fileSize }`. The link expires after a few minutes and was minted for this person: hand it on at once, and call this again for a fresh one. The bytes are not sent here; for a PDF use document-file-get, for the text use document-text-get. Records the access.

operations.name: document-file-get
operations.description: The document’s PDF itself (a stored PDF, or the PDF rendition of an office document), returned as an attached resource (base64 `blob`) up to 5 MiB. A larger file is not sent: read it in pages with document-text-get or get a link with document-download. Only PDFs are served here.

operations.name: document-get
operations.description: One document by id, as the shelf lists it: name, folder, tags, reading status and version summary. Use document-status to follow ingestion and document-text-get for what the file says.

operations.name: document-ingest-cancel
operations.description: Stops a document that is still queued or being read. The document and its file stay; call document-reingest to start over.

operations.name: document-model-get
operations.summary: Read the building model of an IFC document
operations.description: The model record behind an IFC document (processing state and summary), or null when the document is not a model or the IFC feature is off. For model contents use the bim operations.

operations.name: document-move
operations.summary: Move a document to another folder
operations.description: File a document in a folder (`folderId`, from folder-list) or at its shelf’s root with `folderId: null`. Needs write access on the document and on the target folder.

operations.name: document-name-match
operations.summary: Check which file names already exist in a project
operations.description: Before adding files, asks which of the given names a project already holds, with the existing document’s id, size and content hash so identical bytes can be skipped. Read-only.

operations.name: document-preview-get
operations.summary: Get a time-limited preview link for a document
operations.description: Presigns an inline preview of the document: `{ url, contentType, filename, imageUrl, rendition }`. An office document is previewed through its PDF rendition. The URL expires (an hour at most); call again for a fresh one. 415 for content that cannot be previewed, 502 `RENDITION_FAILED` when the conversion failed. No bytes are sent here.

operations.name: document-reingest
operations.description: Queues the document for ingestion once more, for example after a failed read. Follow it with document-status. Needs write access on the document’s project.

operations.name: document-rename
operations.description: Set the name Piloti shows for a document (`displayName`); `null` clears it so the file name shows again. The stored file name never changes. Needs write access to the document’s project or shelf.

operations.name: document-role-clear
operations.description: Removes one role binding; the document itself stays. Binding ids come from document-role-list. Declare the role again with document-role-declare.

operations.name: document-role-declare
operations.summary: Declare a document’s role in a project
operations.description: Binds `documentId` to a `role` of the project's vocabulary (optionally for one `scopeInstanceId`). Your call counts as a person's confirmation. Returns the binding. Document ids come from project-document-list.

operations.name: document-role-list
operations.description: The role bindings of the project (which document is the Baugenehmigung, the Lageplan and so on) in `roles`, plus `missing`: the roles Piloti expects the project to hold and does not. Binding ids feed document-role-clear.

operations.name: document-search
operations.summary: Search a project’s documents by meaning
operations.description: Semantic search over the documents of one project (`projectId`, from project-list) for a question or phrase `q`. Returns the best matching passages with their documents, up to `topK` (default set by the server). Read-only.

operations.name: document-status
operations.description: Where the document is in reading and indexing (queued, processing, ready, failed, held). Poll it after an upload; on a failure call document-reingest, on a stuck run document-ingest-cancel.

operations.name: document-summary-get
operations.summary: Count a project’s documents by state
operations.description: Totals for a project’s shelf (how many documents, in which reading state), matching what the listing shows. Optionally filter by author kind or include archived documents.

operations.name: document-tags-update
operations.summary: Set a document’s tags and topics
operations.description: Replaces the tags of a document with the given list (an empty list clears them); tags must come from the fixed vocabulary. `topics` is optional: leave it out and the model’s topics stay as they are.

operations.name: document-text-get
operations.summary: Read the extracted text of a document
operations.description: A preview of the text Piloti extracted from the document. Use it to see what a file says without opening the file; it is empty until document-status reports the document as read.

operations.name: document-thumbnail-get
operations.description: A time-limited URL of the document’s first-page thumbnail image, `{ url }`, with `url: null` when it has none (not drawn yet, or the file is held by the upload screening). The link expires; no bytes are sent here.

operations.name: document-upload
operations.summary: Upload a file to a project
operations.description: Stores one file in a project (optionally in a folder) and hands it to ingestion. Up to 32 MiB per call through the agent door; the document limit of the office applies too. Send `body.files[0]` as { name, mimeType, contentBase64 } and the route’s text parts in `body.fields` (`projectId` required). Returns the stored document; ingestion runs in the background, follow it with document-status. A file the screening holds comes back held, and a reviewer releases it. Needs write access to the project’s documents.

operations.name: document-version-file-get
operations.description: The bytes of one version (Fassung) of a document under its name, from document-version-list: returned as an attached resource (base64 `blob`) up to 5 MiB; a larger file is not sent, read its text with document-text-get instead. `download: "1"` marks it as an attachment. Only published or superseded versions are served.

operations.name: document-visual-details-get
operations.summary: Read what Piloti saw on a drawing or image
operations.description: The visual reading of a drawing or image document: what the vision model found on its pages. Empty for documents that have no visual reading.

operations.name: hold-create
operations.description: Preserves an entity (`entityType` project, document, conversation, organization, user or folder, and its `entityId`) and blocks its purge, with a `reason`. Needs the compliance permission. Returns the hold; lift it with hold-release.

operations.name: hold-list
operations.description: The open legal holds of the organization, each with its entity, reason and id. Needs the compliance permission. Hold ids feed hold-release.

operations.name: hold-release
operations.description: Lifts a legal hold so the held data can be purged again on its normal schedule. Needs the compliance permission. Hold ids come from hold-list.

operations.name: mail-import-cancel
operations.description: Cancels an import and discards the parts already sent. Only the person who started it, or an org project administrator, may cancel. Import ids come from mail-import-list.

operations.name: mail-import-complete
operations.description: Call once every part is sent: the parts are joined and the filing job is queued (HTTP 202). Answers the import with its status; follow it with mail-import-get. Refused with 409 when the import was cancelled meanwhile, and with 400 when a part is missing.

operations.name: mail-import-get
operations.description: One Outlook archive import, as the upload plan: which parts the store already holds. Use it to check progress or to resume a send that broke off. Import ids come from mail-import-list.

operations.name: mail-import-list
operations.description: The project's Outlook archive imports with their status and counts. Import ids feed mail-import-get and mail-import-cancel.

operations.name: mail-import-part-upload
operations.summary: Send one part of an Outlook archive
operations.description: Sends the raw bytes of part `partNumber` (1-based) of the archive started with mail-import-start, as `body.contentBase64`. Every part must be exactly the plan’s `partSize` bytes, the last one the remainder, or the route answers 400 with the size it expected. Sending a part again replaces it, so a broken send resumes: read mail-import-get for `uploadedParts` and send the rest. Only the person who started the import may send. Returns `{ partNumber }`.

operations.name: mail-import-start
operations.description: Registers a .pst or .ost archive for import into the project (`filename`, `sizeBytes`) and answers the upload plan `{ import, partSize, partCount, uploadedParts }`. Then send the archive in `partCount` parts of exactly `partSize` bytes (the last one shorter) with mail-import-part-upload, and finish with mail-import-complete. Needs the mail-import feature and write access to the project’s documents. Archives are large (up to 25 GB); each part is a 32 MiB call.

operations.name: office-shelf-document-delete
operations.description: Deletes one Büroablage document for good: its stored file, its search chunks and its record. This cannot be undone. Needs org:office_shelf:manage. Document ids come from office-shelf-document-list.

operations.name: office-shelf-document-list
operations.description: One page of the office-wide Büroablage documents, same rows and filters as project-document-list but without `projectId`: `folderId`, `sort`, `dir`, `q`, `state`, `limit`, `includeArchived`, `authoredBy`. Follow `nextCursor` (pass it as `cursor`) until it is null. Document ids from here feed the document operations.

operations.name: office-shelf-document-lookup
operations.summary: Find Büroablage documents by file name
operations.description: Resolves exact file names (case-insensitive) to their Büroablage document rows. Use it when you have names, for example from a citation, and need ids. Names without a match are simply absent from `documents`.

operations.name: office-shelf-document-name-probe
operations.summary: Check which file names the Büroablage holds
operations.description: Given file names about to be uploaded, returns the Büroablage documents that already carry them. Call it before an upload to avoid duplicates. Changes nothing.

operations.name: office-shelf-document-revision-probe
operations.summary: Find documents a file name would revise
operations.description: Given dropped file names, returns the Büroablage documents each would be the next Fassung of, so the upload can file it as a new version instead of a second document. Changes nothing.

operations.name: office-shelf-document-search
operations.description: Document-centric semantic search over the office's shared Büroablage. `q` is a natural-language query, `topK` (1 to 100) caps the hits. Returns the best matching documents. For the project's own documents use the knowledge operations.

operations.name: office-shelf-document-summary
operations.description: What the database can say about every Büroablage document at once: counts per folder by read-state family, plus the failed documents. Cheaper than paging office-shelf-document-list when you need an overview.

operations.name: office-shelf-document-upload
operations.summary: Upload a file to the Büroablage
operations.description: Stores one file in the office-wide Büroablage (optionally in one of its folders) and ingests it into the shared collection. Up to 32 MiB per call through the agent door; the document limit of the office applies too. Send `body.files[0]` as { name, mimeType, contentBase64 }. Needs the right to manage the Büroablage. Returns the stored document; follow ingestion with document-status.

operations.name: project-document-list
operations.description: One page of the project's documents with name, folder, author, lifecycle and version state. Pass `projectId` (from project-list). Without level parameters it drains the whole shelf, 500 a page; `folderId` (a folder id or `root`), `sort`, `dir`, `q`, `state` or `limit` read one folder level instead. Follow `nextCursor` (pass it as `cursor`) until it is null.

operations.name: project-upload-list
operations.description: Who brought how many files into the project when, and how each upload ended, one page at a time; follow `nextCursor` (pass it as `cursor`) until it is null. Per-file detail is in upload-batch-get, which only the uploader may read.

operations.name: quarantine-list
operations.description: Documents the content check held back that the person may release or delete: org admins see the organization's queue, project admins their projects' part, everyone else an empty `items` list.

operations.name: session-document-upload
operations.summary: Attach a file to a conversation
operations.description: Stores one file privately on one conversation (not in any project shelf) and ingests it for that chat. Up to 32 MiB per call through the agent door; the document limit of the office applies too. Send `body.files[0]` as { name, mimeType, contentBase64 } and `body.fields.conversationId`; the conversation is created when it does not exist yet. Returns the stored document; follow ingestion with document-status.

operations.name: upload-batch-get
operations.description: What arrived in one upload, where it was filed, what each file is and what was held back and why. Only the uploader may read it; anyone else is answered as if it did not exist.

operations.name: upload-batch-open
operations.description: Announces an upload before its first file: pass a fresh uuid `id`, the `scope` (project, office_shelf or session), `projectId` for a project upload, and `expectedCount`. The server then knows when all files are read and keeps the upload history. Seal it with upload-batch-seal after the last file.

operations.name: upload-batch-seal
operations.description: Closes an upload batch after the last file: `unchanged` and `failed` count the files that wrote no row, `excluded` the names the screening refused as terms and counts. Only the uploader may seal. The id is the one given to upload-batch-open.

operations.name: office-shelf-folder-create
operations.description: Creates one folder under `parentId` (null or absent: the shelf root). Needs org:office_shelf:manage. Refused when a sibling has the name; use office-shelf-folder-ensure to get-or-create paths. Returns `{ folder }`.

operations.name: office-shelf-folder-delete
operations.description: Deletes the folder; its documents and subfolders are re-filed one level up, not deleted. Returns `{ documentsMoved, foldersMoved }`. Folder ids come from office-shelf-folder-list. Needs org:office_shelf:manage.

operations.name: office-shelf-folder-ensure
operations.summary: Resolve Büroablage folder paths, creating the missing
operations.description: Takes directory paths (relative to `parentId`, null: the shelf root), returns the folders plus `folderIdByPath`, and creates whatever is missing. An existing folder counts as success. Needs org:office_shelf:manage. Safe to repeat.

operations.name: office-shelf-folder-list
operations.description: Every folder of the office-wide Büroablage (office shelf), in the same shape as project-folder-list. Any member may read. Folder ids feed office-shelf-folder-update, office-shelf-folder-delete and the `folderId` filter of office-shelf-document-list.

operations.name: office-shelf-folder-update
operations.summary: Rename, move or describe a Büroablage folder
operations.description: Changes a folder's `name`, `parentId` (null moves it to the shelf root) or `description` (null clears it); send only what changes. Folder ids come from office-shelf-folder-list. Needs org:office_shelf:manage. Returns `{ folder }`.

operations.name: project-folder-access-get
operations.summary: Read who may open a project folder
operations.description: The folder’s access as it is now: `{ mode: "inherit" }`, or `{ mode: "custom", everyoneReads, people: [{ userId, level }] }`. Needs manage rights on the project and write access on the folder, as a change would. Change it with project-folder-access-set. Folder ids come from project-folder-list.

operations.name: project-folder-bin-list
operations.description: The project's Papierkorb: the deleted folders the person may read, who deleted each and when, when its purge runs, and what the person may do about it (restore, purge now). Folder ids from here feed project-folder-restore and project-folder-bin-purge.

operations.name: project-folder-bin-purge
operations.summary: Purge a folder from the bin now
operations.description: Deletes a binned folder for good, with its subfolders and documents, instead of waiting for the grace period. This cannot be undone. Needs project:manage; a legal hold refuses it with 409 without naming the hold. Folder ids come from project-folder-bin-list.

operations.name: project-folder-create
operations.summary: Create a folder in a project
operations.description: Creates one folder under `parentId` (null or absent: the project root). Refused with a message when a sibling already has the name; to get-or-create whole paths use project-folder-ensure. Returns `{ folder }`. Needs write access on the parent folder.

operations.name: project-folder-delete
operations.summary: Move a project folder to the bin
operations.description: Moves the folder with its subfolders and documents to the project's Papierkorb. It stays restorable (project-folder-restore) until the `purgeAfter` date the response names, then is purged. Returns `{ documentsBinned, foldersBinned, purgeAfter }`. Needs write access on the folder and everything below it.

operations.name: project-folder-ensure
operations.summary: Resolve folder paths, creating the missing
operations.description: Takes directory paths (relative to `parentId`, null: the project root) and returns the folders plus `folderIdByPath`, creating whatever is missing. Unlike project-folder-create it treats an existing folder as success, so call it before filing documents into a tree. Safe to repeat.

operations.name: project-folder-list
operations.description: Every folder of the project's Dateien that the person may read, each with its id, name, parent, path and the person's own access, plus `rootAccess` (what they may do at the project root). Folder ids from here feed project-folder-update, project-folder-delete, document filters (`folderId` of project-document-list) and the `parentId` of project-folder-create.

operations.name: project-folder-restore
operations.summary: Restore a folder from the bin
operations.description: Brings a deleted folder back with its access, subfolders and documents. The response says `restoredTo: 'root'` when its former parent no longer exists. Folder ids come from project-folder-bin-list.

operations.name: project-folder-update
operations.summary: Rename, move or describe a project folder
operations.description: Changes a folder's `name`, its `parentId` (null moves it to the project root) or its `description` (null clears it); send only what changes. Folder ids come from project-folder-list. A move that changes who can open the subtree also needs project:manage. Returns `{ folder }`.

operations.name: annotation-create
operations.summary: Place an annotation on a document
operations.description: Sets a new mark at a place on the document (page position or text range, as the schema describes) with a kind and a body. Returns the annotation with its number. Colleagues named in `mentions` are told.

operations.name: annotation-delete
operations.summary: Delete one of your own annotations
operations.description: Removes a mark its author set. A mark that has been discussed or carried to another Fassung is refused with a 409; resolve it instead (annotation-update). Deleting cannot be undone.

operations.name: annotation-get
operations.summary: Read one annotation with its thread
operations.description: One Anmerkung with its whole reply thread, status and carry links (id from annotation-list).

operations.name: annotation-list
operations.summary: List the annotations on a document
operations.description: Every Anmerkung (mark) on the document with its place, status, assignee and replies, including Piloti’s open proposals. The ids feed annotation-get, annotation-update and annotation-reply-create.

operations.name: annotation-reply-create
operations.description: Adds a reply to an annotation. Set `addressesPiloti` or mention Piloti to ask it to answer. Returns the annotation with its thread.

operations.name: annotation-reply-delete
operations.summary: Take back one of your own replies
operations.description: Deletes a reply its author wrote, while the mark is live and Piloti has not taken it up (otherwise a 409). It cannot be undone.

operations.name: annotation-reply-update
operations.summary: Reword one of your own replies
operations.description: Rewords a reply its author wrote, while the mark is live and Piloti has not taken it up (otherwise a 409). Returns the annotation with its thread.

operations.name: annotation-update
operations.summary: Change, resolve or reassign an annotation
operations.description: Edits a mark: reword it, assign it, set a due day, or move its status (open, resolved, dismissed). Send at least one field. `expectedStatus` guards against overwriting a colleague’s change; `carryToCurrent` carries an open mark onto the current Fassung.

operations.name: document-annotations-export
operations.summary: Export a document’s annotations as a Protokoll file
operations.description: The document’s Anmerkungen as one file: PDF (default), Word (docx) or Markdown (md), the open ones or all, for the current Fassung or every one. Returned as an attached resource up to 5 MiB; Markdown comes back as text. Records an audit event. For the data itself use annotation-list. Needs read access to the document.

operations.name: document-quarantine-get
operations.summary: Read why a document is held and who may release it
operations.description: For a document held by upload screening: the reason and what the caller may do (request release, or release it as a reviewer). Next: document-quarantine-release-request or document-quarantine-release.

operations.name: document-quarantine-release
operations.description: A reviewer lets a held file through screening so it is read and shown like any other document. Needs the reviewer permission (see document-quarantine-get). Send no body; the release is recorded and cannot be taken back.

operations.name: document-quarantine-release-request
operations.summary: Ask a reviewer to release a held upload
operations.description: The uploader asks the project’s reviewers to release their held file. Notifies the reviewers; changes nothing about the file itself. Send no body.

operations.name: document-revision-candidates
operations.summary: Find documents a new file could replace
operations.description: For file names about to be added to a project (`projectId`, `names`, optional target `folders`), lists existing documents each could be a new Fassung of. Read-only; feeds document-revision-link-set.

operations.name: document-revision-compare
operations.summary: Compare a document visually with the one it replaces
operations.description: Marks what changed on one page between the older document (`older`, an id) and this newer one: boxed regions plus short sentences. Read-only; both documents must be readable and screened. Candidates for `older` come from document-revision-candidates.

operations.name: document-revision-link-set
operations.summary: Confirm or take back a Fassung link
operations.description: States that this document replaces `older` (`linked: true`) or takes that link back (`linked: false`). Both documents must be in the same collection and the caller needs write access.

operations.name: document-thread-ensure
operations.summary: Open the caller’s chat thread about a document
operations.description: Returns the id of the caller’s own conversation about this document, creating it (with an optional `title`) the first time. Use the conversation operations with that id to read or post in it.

operations.name: document-version-approve
operations.description: Records the reviewer’s approval of a version in review. `ifMatch` is the `contentHash` the reviewer read; a mismatch is a 409. Next: document-version-publish makes an approved version current.

operations.name: document-version-content-get
operations.summary: Read the text of a version
operations.description: The full text of one version of a draft-type document, as plain text. Use document-version-diff to compare two versions.

operations.name: document-version-content-replace
operations.summary: Replace the text of a draft version
operations.description: Writes the whole body of a draft version. `ifMatch` is the `contentHash` you last read (document-version-get); a mismatch is a 409 and nothing is overwritten. Only drafts are editable. Next: document-version-submit.

operations.name: document-version-diff
operations.summary: Compare the text of two versions
operations.description: Returns both versions (state and full text) side by side so you can see what changed between `from` and `to`. Both ids come from document-version-list.

operations.name: document-version-fork
operations.summary: Start a new draft from the published version
operations.description: Forks an editable draft from the document’s published version and returns it. Send an empty body. Next: document-version-content-replace to write the draft, then document-version-submit to send it to review.

operations.name: document-version-get
operations.description: One version of a document: lifecycle state, author, reviewers, decisions and `contentHash` (the `ifMatch` value for edits and decisions).

operations.name: document-version-list
operations.description: Every version (Fassung) of a document with its lifecycle state, author and content hash. Start here to get a `versionId` for the other document-version operations.

operations.name: document-version-publish
operations.description: Makes an approved version the document’s current published Fassung; the previous published version is superseded. Send no body.

operations.name: document-version-reject
operations.description: Refuses a version in review. A `comment` saying why is required; `ifMatch` is the `contentHash` the reviewer read.

operations.name: document-version-request-changes
operations.summary: Ask for changes on a version under review
operations.description: Sends a version in review back for rework. A `comment` is required; set `delegateRevision` to hand the rework to Piloti as a task instead of leaving it with the author.

operations.name: document-version-reviewer-list
operations.summary: List who can be asked to review a document
operations.description: The colleagues who hold edit rights on the document’s project and can be named as reviewers. Their user ids go into `reviewerUserIds` of document-version-submit.

operations.name: document-version-submit
operations.summary: Send a draft version to review
operations.description: Submits a draft for review. `reviewerUserIds` names who is asked (from document-version-reviewer-list; empty asks the item’s assignees), `orderMessage` is the one-sentence order and `dueAt` an optional date. Reviewers then call document-version-approve, -reject or -request-changes.

operations.name: project-annotation-list
operations.description: The project's Offene Punkte: the live Anmerkungen across every document the person may see, a page at a time. Filter with `status` (open, proposed, all-live), `assignee` (me or a user id), `due` (overdue, soon) and `order`; follow `nextCursor` (pass it as `cursor`).

operations.name: project-annotations-export
operations.summary: Export a project’s open points as a Protokoll file
operations.description: The project’s Offene Punkte as one Protokoll: PDF (default), Word (docx) or Markdown (md), filtered like project-annotation-list (`status`, `assignee`, `due`, `order`). Returned as an attached resource up to 5 MiB; Markdown comes back as text. Refused when more than 1000 marks match: narrow the filters. Records an audit event.

operations.name: answer-feedback-list
operations.summary: Read the person’s votes in a conversation
operations.description: The thumbs-up and thumbs-down votes the person has given to answers in one conversation (conversationId from conversation-list). Only their own votes are returned.

operations.name: answer-feedback-retract
operations.summary: Take back a vote on an answer
operations.description: Removes the person’s vote on one answer (messageId from answer-feedback-list). Nothing happens if there is no vote.

operations.name: answer-feedback-submit
operations.description: Records a verdict on one answer (messageId from conversation-message-list). Voting again replaces the earlier vote. A down-vote feeds Piloti’s failure learning, so add the reason when the answer was wrong.

operations.name: citation-format
operations.summary: Format sources as APA, BibTeX or RIS
operations.description: Renders CSL-JSON `items` (the sources of an answer, up to 64) as an APA bibliography, BibTeX or RIS text. Pure formatting: nothing is read or stored. Returns `{ text }`.

operations.name: conversation-create
operations.description: Creates an empty private conversation, optionally inside a project (projectId from project-list) or about one document. You choose the id: `s_` followed by a UUID with underscores for the hyphens. Returns the conversation. Share it deliberately afterwards (sharing-get shows who has access).

operations.name: conversation-delete
operations.description: Deletes a conversation and its messages for everyone in it. This cannot be undone. The answer is the same whether or not the id existed or was the person’s, so it never reveals which ids are real.

operations.name: conversation-draft-file
operations.summary: File an unfiled draft into the project
operations.description: Files the content of a draft (path from the answer’s card or conversation-draft-get) as a document in the conversation’s project, as the person. A same-name collision answers 409 with the existing document; repeat with `force: true` only after the person confirmed filing anyway. Returns the filed document.

operations.name: conversation-draft-get
operations.summary: Read an unfiled draft Piloti wrote
operations.description: The content of one draft in the conversation’s working directory, so it can be read before filing. `path` is the draft path the answer’s card names (such as `/entwuerfe/….md`). Read-only. To keep it, call conversation-draft-file.

operations.name: conversation-get
operations.description: One conversation by id: title, project, visibility, engagement mode (when Piloti answers) and the person’s role in it. Messages come from conversation-message-list.

operations.name: conversation-list
operations.summary: List the conversations the person can see
operations.description: Every conversation the person may open, their own and those shared with them, newest first, with id, title, project and unread state. Pass projectId to narrow to one project (ids from project-list). Take a conversation id from here for conversation-get and conversation-message-list.

operations.name: conversation-message-add
operations.summary: Store a message in a conversation
operations.description: Appends one message, or an array of up to the per-request limit, to a thread the person may write in. You supply each message id. Use `mentions` (user ids from conversation-mention-candidate-list) to address colleagues; they get an inbox item. This stores the message only: it does not open a turn with Piloti, which runs over the chat WebSocket. Returns the stored rows with the addressee ruling.

operations.name: conversation-message-changes
operations.description: The changes Piloti made while producing one answer, each as it stands now, with `canUndo`. Changes on documents the person may not see are left out. Pass a change id to piloti-change-undo to reverse it.

operations.name: conversation-message-export
operations.summary: Export one saved answer as a Word document
operations.description: One answer of a conversation as a .docx, built from the stored message with its sources. Returned as an attached resource (base64 `blob`) up to 5 MiB. Needs access to the conversation. Message ids come from conversation-message-list; only an answer from Piloti can be exported.

operations.name: conversation-message-list
operations.summary: Read the messages of a conversation
operations.description: The whole history of a conversation, oldest first: each message with id, role, content, structured mentions and the answer details Piloti stored. Message ids from here feed conversation-message-changes and conversation-message-usage.

operations.name: conversation-message-update
operations.summary: Record a card decision or details on an answer
operations.description: Saves the person’s decisions on an answer’s interactive cards (`cardInteractions`, keyed like `memory_proposal-0`) and the answer’s own details (`provenance`, `promptState`, `stages`). Provide at least one field. The service whitelists the free-form parts; to act on a proposal use proposal-apply instead.

operations.name: conversation-message-usage
operations.description: The credits billed for one answer (or tokens, on the organization’s own key) with the token split. Returns `{ usage: null }` when no ledger row names the answer.

operations.name: conversation-read-mark
operations.description: Moves the person’s read marker to now, or to `lastReadMessageId`, and clears the thread’s inbox items. Read state is per person. Send an empty object to mark everything read.

operations.name: conversation-title-generate
operations.description: Generates a short title and topic tags from the opening exchange (up to 20 messages with role and content) and saves them on the conversation. Pass `locale` for the title’s language. Returns the stored title.

operations.name: conversation-update
operations.summary: Rename a conversation or change when Piloti answers
operations.description: Set a new `title` (needs the owner role) and/or the `engagement` mode that decides when Piloti answers (needs the collaborator role). Provide at least one of the two. Returns the updated conversation.

operations.name: feedback-report-submit
operations.summary: Send product feedback to the Piloti team
operations.description: Sends a bug report, idea, praise or question to the platform owners (`kind` and `message`, plus the `pagePath` it concerns). Opens a support ticket. This is not an answer vote: use answer-feedback-submit for that. Rate limited per person.

operations.name: passage-similar-search
operations.summary: Find passages like one in the office’s documents
operations.description: Given a passage the person is reading (its document by id or by legal-corpus file name, and its text), finds similar passages across the projects and documents they may read, grouped project, document, passage. Read-only. Use it to see how the office handled the same question before.

operations.name: assignment-add
operations.summary: Assign a person to a resource
operations.description: Puts a person (`userId` from assignment-candidate-list) on the hook for the resource. Assignment is not access. Needs the collaborator role. Returns the updated assignees.

operations.name: assignment-candidate-list
operations.summary: List who can be assigned to a resource
operations.description: Project members who may be assigned. With `access: write` (documents only) only people who may change the document, which is who an annotation may be handed to. User ids from here feed assignment-add.

operations.name: assignment-list
operations.summary: List who a resource is assigned to
operations.description: The people currently assigned to a shareable resource, as `{ assignees }`.

operations.name: assignment-remove
operations.summary: Release a person from a resource
operations.description: Removes the assignment of `userId` (from assignment-list). Returns the updated assignees.

operations.name: conversation-awaiting-get
operations.summary: See whom a conversation is waiting on
operations.description: The open mention requests on a conversation: the hand-offs where the thread waits for a colleague. Request ids feed mention-request-release.

operations.name: conversation-mention-candidate-list
operations.summary: List who can be mentioned in a conversation
operations.description: The people (and Piloti) a message in this conversation may mention. Mentions are structured: use the `targetId` values from here in conversation-message-add, never a name typed in text.

operations.name: inbox-item-archive
operations.description: Puts one inbox item (id from inbox-list) away. The row survives and can be brought back with inbox-item-restore.

operations.name: inbox-item-mark-read
operations.description: Marks read by `itemIds` (from inbox-list), or everything with `{ all: true }`, or the news on one document mark (`resourceType`, `resourceId`, `anchorId`), or the “new marks” rows of a document (`marksSet: true`). Returns the recomputed badge count.

operations.name: inbox-item-mark-unread
operations.description: The inverse of inbox-item-mark-read for `itemIds` from inbox-list. Returns the recomputed badge count.

operations.name: inbox-item-restore
operations.summary: Take an inbox item out of the archive
operations.description: Brings an archived inbox item (id from inbox-list with filter `archived`) back into the inbox.

operations.name: inbox-list
operations.description: One page of the person’s own inbox. `filter` picks the slice: `requests` waits on them, `unread`, `all` (everything unarchived, the default), `archived`, `pending`. Pass the previous page’s `nextCursor` as `cursor` for the next page. Item ids feed the inbox-item-* operations.

operations.name: inbox-summary-get
operations.description: Only the number of items waiting on the person, as the inbox badge shows it. Cheaper than inbox-list.

operations.name: inbox-unread-anchor-list
operations.summary: List unread marks inside a document
operations.description: The ids of the marks (anchors) in one document whose news the person has not read, as `{ anchorIds }`. resourceId is a document id from document-list. Opening a mark’s thread clears it (inbox-item-mark-read).

operations.name: mention-request-release
operations.summary: Carry on without the person a thread waits on
operations.description: Releases an open hand-off (request id from conversation-awaiting-get) so the thread no longer waits. Any contributor may do it. The mentioned colleague’s inbox item is settled.

operations.name: piloti-change-undo
operations.description: Reverses one change Piloti applied (id from conversation-message-changes). Answers 409 with `moved-on` if the object has changed since, or `already-undone`. The inverse runs with the person’s own rights.

operations.name: proposal-apply
operations.description: Carries out a proposal that is still `proposed` as the person (409 otherwise) and returns it with its `results`. The body is optional; `memoryScope: project` keeps a proposed note on the project. Needs the right the proposal’s kind requires. Reverse it with piloti-change-undo where the result allows.

operations.name: proposal-dismiss
operations.description: Rejects a proposal that is still `proposed` (409 otherwise). Nothing is changed in the workspace.

operations.name: proposal-get
operations.description: One proposal as the person may see it, with `canDecide` telling whether they may apply or dismiss it.

operations.name: proposal-list
operations.summary: List open proposed changes on a shelf
operations.description: Piloti’s open proposals (file operations, notes, profile changes) with the documents they name. Give `projectId` (from project-list) for a project, or `shelf: office_shelf` for the office shelf, and optionally `kind`. Ids feed proposal-get, proposal-apply and proposal-dismiss.

operations.name: push-device-list
operations.summary: List the devices that receive push notifications
operations.description: The person’s own registered browsers and devices. Ids feed push-device-remove.

operations.name: push-device-remove
operations.summary: Stop push notifications to one device
operations.description: Removes one of the person’s own devices (id from push-device-list). It receives no more pushes.

operations.name: push-preference-get
operations.description: What the person wants pushed (the categories requests, results, access, activity, office) and whether the lock screen shows content. Defaults are filled in.

operations.name: push-preference-update
operations.description: Sets `showContent` and/or any of the `categories` booleans; fields left out stay as they are. Returns the resolved preferences.

operations.name: session-document-delete
operations.summary: Remove a file attached to a conversation
operations.description: Deletes one chat attachment (id from session-document-list) with its retrieval chunks and stored copies. This cannot be undone. Needs the collaborator role on the conversation.

operations.name: session-document-list
operations.summary: List the files attached to a conversation
operations.description: The documents attached privately to one conversation (conversationId from conversation-list). Read, preview or download them through the document operations.

operations.name: sharing-candidate-list
operations.summary: List who could be invited to a resource
operations.description: Organization members who may be invited to the resource, plus those flagged `needsProjectAccess` because they would first need to join the project. Only the resource owner may read it.

operations.name: sharing-get
operations.summary: Read who has access to a resource
operations.description: The sharing state of a conversation or other shareable resource: its visibility, the people with a grant and their roles, and the person’s own role. Change it with sharing-visibility-set, sharing-grant-add, sharing-grant-update and sharing-grant-revoke.

operations.name: user-preference-get
operations.description: The person’s own preference bag (language, active project and other UI settings) as `{ prefs }`.

operations.name: user-preference-update
operations.description: Merges `prefs` into the person’s preference bag; keys not named stay. Setting `locale` also switches the interface language. Returns the merged `{ prefs }`.

operations.name: job-create
operations.summary: Create a standing or one-off job
operations.description: Create a job in a project: a name, a prompt, optionally an attached skill (skill-list), data sources and either a 5-field cron schedule with an IANA timezone or a one-time `dueAt` (not both; neither means it runs only by hand with job-run). Needs project:skills:manage. Returns `{ job }` with its id.

operations.name: job-delete
operations.description: Delete a job and stop its schedule. Needs project:skills:manage. To keep the job but stop it firing, call job-update with `enabled: false` instead.

operations.name: job-get
operations.description: One job by id: name, prompt, attached skill, data sources, schedule (cron and timezone, or a due time), enabled flag and next run. For what it produced, call job-run-list.

operations.name: job-list
operations.description: The jobs of one project: scheduled or one-off prompts Piloti runs as a research run that files a report, with their schedule, attached skill and next run. Needs the skills feature on. Take a job id from here for job-get, job-update, job-delete, job-run and job-run-list.

operations.name: job-run
operations.description: Fire a job immediately, outside its schedule ("Run now"). Fails with 409 when the job is disabled; when the backend is at capacity the run comes back as `skipped` rather than failing. Needs project:skills:manage. Follow the result with run-get using the run id it returns.

operations.name: job-run-list
operations.summary: List the runs of a job
operations.description: The submission history of one job, newest first, paginated with `limit` (1 to 200, default 50) and `offset`. Use it to see whether a scheduled job fired and how each run ended.

operations.name: job-update
operations.description: Patch any of a job’s name, prompt, attached skill, data sources, enabled flag, schedule or due time. Changing the skill re-resolves it and changing the schedule recomputes the next run. Set `enabled: false` to pause a job without deleting it. Needs project:skills:manage.

operations.name: run-cancel
operations.description: Ask the backend to stop one run. Refuses with 409 when the run can no longer be stopped. Returns the run view as it stands; the ledger turns `cancelled` afterwards, so read it again with run-get.

operations.name: run-commission
operations.description: Start a deep research run for a question inside an existing conversation of the project: `conversationId` (from conversation-list), `question`, optional `context` and optional `documents` ({ basis, excluded } lists of document names) to carry forward. Needs the deep-research feature and collaborator access to the conversation. Returns `{ runId, runMessageId, conversationId, status }`; follow it with run-get.

operations.name: run-document-add
operations.summary: Add a document to a running run’s basis
operations.description: Name one more document (`name` as the inventory lists it, optional `title` and `shelf`) for a running run to read in full. Documents from a restricted folder are refused. Returns the run view.

operations.name: run-get
operations.description: One run by its public id: where its message sits in the conversation and what its ledger says (phase, status, the documents it reads). Poll it after run-commission or job-run. Needs project:view.

operations.name: run-write-now
operations.summary: Tell a run to write its report now
operations.description: Stop a research run gathering sources and make it write the report from what it has ("Jetzt schreiben"). Returns the run view; read it again with run-get to see the report arrive.

operations.name: task-list
operations.description: The project’s delegated work, newest first: each task with its status, the job it came from and its review state. Needs the skills and task-automation features on. A finished task awaits task-review.

operations.name: task-review
operations.summary: Accept or reject a finished task
operations.description: Record a person’s verdict on a finished task: `decision` accepts or rejects it, and a rejection can carry a `reason` that the next run of the same job is told. Needs project:edit. Task ids come from task-list. Returns `{ task }`.

operations.name: skill-category-create
operations.description: Add an organization category with a `name`, optional `description` and `sortOrder`. Needs org:skills:manage. Returns the new category with its id.

operations.name: skill-category-delete
operations.description: Remove one of the organization’s categories. Platform categories answer 404 here. Needs org:skills:manage.

operations.name: skill-category-list
operations.description: The categories that arrange the toolbox: platform categories first (read-only), then the organization’s own. Category ids feed skill-create, skill-update and the category operations.

operations.name: skill-category-update
operations.description: Rename, re-describe or re-order one of the organization’s categories. Platform categories answer 404 here. Needs org:skills:manage.

operations.name: skill-create
operations.description: Create a skill for the organization: lowercase hyphenated `name`, `description`, markdown `body`, and optionally `metadata`, `enabled`, `categoryId` (skill-category-list) or `clonedFrom` (a platform skill name). Needs org:skills:manage. Try skill-review on a draft first.

operations.name: skill-curated-set-enabled
operations.summary: Switch a platform skill on or off
operations.description: Turn a platform-curated skill on or off for this organization. Addressed by NAME (from skill-list), because a platform skill has no id; only curated skills can be switched, never the pipeline’s own machinery. Needs org:skills:manage.

operations.name: skill-delete
operations.description: Delete one of the organization’s own skills. Jobs that name it lose their attachment. Needs org:skills:manage. To switch a skill off while keeping it, use skill-update with `enabled: false`.

operations.name: skill-invocable-list
operations.summary: List the skills a chat turn may invoke
operations.description: The skills this member may invoke in a chat turn, name and description only (no bodies): the catalogue behind the composer’s "/" menu and the one the agent is given at turn start.

operations.name: skill-list
operations.summary: List the skills of the toolbox
operations.description: The organization’s skill toolbox: platform-curated skills and the organization’s own, each with its name, description, category and whether it is enabled. Needs the skills feature on. Org skill ids from here feed skill-update and skill-delete; names feed job-create.

operations.name: skill-review
operations.summary: Have the reviewer critique a skill draft
operations.description: Ask the backend reviewer what is wrong with a skill draft. Send whatever of `name`, `description` and `body` exists; an incomplete draft is fine. Answers 200 with `{ findings, error? }`; null findings means no review this time, not a pass. Changes nothing.

operations.name: skill-update
operations.description: Patch any of an org skill’s name, description, body, metadata, enabled flag or category (`categoryId: null` removes it from its category). Platform skills have no id here; use skill-curated-set-enabled for those. Needs org:skills:manage.

operations.name: address-search
operations.description: Search public map data for an address (`q`, at least 3 characters; `limit` caps results). Answers `{ enabled, results }`; `enabled: false` means no geocoding provider is configured. Use it to resolve an address before creating a project.

operations.name: knowledge-base-get
operations.summary: See what the building-law corpus contains
operations.description: The status of the platform-owned base corpus (OIB guidelines and the like): which documents it holds and whether they are indexed. Identical for every organization. To search the corpus, ask a question in a conversation; this only lists what is there.

operations.name: knowledge-document-get
operations.description: The PDF of one document of the building-law base corpus (the file names are listed by knowledge-base-get), returned as an attached resource up to 5 MiB; a larger file is not sent. Identical for every organization. Use it to quote a source a citation points at.

operations.name: ris-document-get
operations.summary: Read the text of a RIS legal document
operations.description: Fetch the text of an Austrian RIS document from a citation: `reference` is a document number (NOR40217157) or a https://www.ris.bka.gv.at/ URL, `application` disambiguates a bare number, and `passage` windows a long document around the cited passage. Answers 404 when RIS serves no text for it and 502 when RIS is unreachable. Rate limited.

operations.name: widget-token-get
operations.summary: Mint a short-lived WorkOS widget token
operations.description: A user-specific, short-lived WorkOS widget authorization token (never cache it) for the requested `scope` values; scopes the person does not hold are dropped. `org=platform` asks for the platform organization and is guarded. Returns `{ token }`. Only useful to a client that renders WorkOS widgets.

operations.name: bim-check-confirm
operations.summary: Confirm an OIB rule for a model revision
operations.description: Record that the person has judged `ruleId` satisfied for the model revision `modelId` (bim-model-list), with an optional `note`. The confirming identity is the signed-in person, never the body. Needs project:edit. Only call it on the person’s explicit judgement.

operations.name: bim-check-list
operations.summary: List the human verdicts on the OIB rules
operations.description: The confirmations people recorded for a project’s OIB rule catalogue: which rule, which model revision, who confirmed it and the note. These settle what the model’s published values cannot. Needs project:view.

operations.name: bim-check-withdraw
operations.description: Take back the confirmation of `ruleId` for one model revision `modelId`; confirmations are keyed per revision, so both are required. Needs project:edit. Re-confirm with bim-check-confirm.

operations.name: bim-checks-export
operations.summary: Export the Prüfbuch as a BCF archive
operations.description: The project’s OIB rule check ledger for one model as a BCF 2.1 zip, one topic per finding. Name the model with `modelId` (a uuid) or `model` (its file name), and state `buildingClass` (1 to 5) and `mainUse` so rules that need them do not stand down. Returned as an attached resource up to 5 MiB; a larger archive is not sent (ask for the findings with bim-check-list). The most expensive read in the product: it runs the whole catalogue and is rate limited. Needs the ifc-models feature.

operations.name: bim-model-get
operations.description: One model’s header and summary: spatial tree, storeys, element type counts and totals. Start here to learn what is in a model, then ask exact questions with bim-model-query.

operations.name: bim-model-list
operations.summary: List the BIM models in scope for a project
operations.description: The IFC models a project can use: its own uploads plus the organization Archiv’s, each with its id, name and revision. Needs the ifc-models feature. Model ids feed bim-model-get, bim-model-query and bim-check-confirm.

operations.name: bim-model-query
operations.summary: Ask a structured question of a BIM model
operations.description: Run one deterministic query against one model, as numbers and rows rather than prose: the body is a closed vocabulary selected by `op` (overview, health, schedule, compliance, compliance-diff, profile, takeoff, compare, types, elements, element, properties, aggregate). Use it for every count, sum and filter ("how many external walls on the ground floor"); never estimate such answers. Changes nothing. Get the model id from bim-model-list.

operations.name: bim-model-source-get
operations.summary: Get a time-limited link to a model’s IFC file
operations.description: A presigned URL of the raw .ifc, valid for ten minutes and minted for this person only: treat it as a credential, do not store or share it, and call again for a fresh one. The file itself is not sent (models run to hundreds of MB); open the link, or ask exact questions with bim-model-query. Needs the ifc-models feature. Get the model id from bim-model-list.

operations.name: diagram-file
operations.summary: File a drawn diagram into a project
operations.description: File a diagram as documents of the project: the `svg` and its `source` (mermaid or excalidraw), a `title`, and `runId`, the id of the chat answer it was drawn in (filing the same diagram twice files nothing twice). Optionally `conversationId` so restricted-folder rules apply. Returns `{ svg, pdf }`, `pdf` null when only the SVG landed. Needs project:documents:write and project:documents:generate.

operations.name: organization-budget-get
operations.description: Daily and monthly limits (credits, or tokens for an organization on its own key) for the organization and the caller; budget admins also get every member and project limit. Change with organization-budget-set, remove a member or project limit with organization-budget-remove.

operations.name: organization-budget-remove
operations.summary: Remove a member or project budget limit
operations.description: Deletes the limit of one member or one project so that the organization limits alone apply. The organization limits themselves are changed with organization-budget-set. subjectId is a user id from organization-member-list or a project id from project-list.

operations.name: organization-budget-set
operations.description: Sets the daily and monthly limit (null means unlimited) for the organization, one member or one project. The unit follows the organization’s key mode. Organization and member scopes need budget admin rights; project scope also works for that project’s admins. subjectId is a user id from organization-member-list or a project id from project-list; omit it for the organization scope.

operations.name: organization-deleted-folder-content-get
operations.description: Who may still see chats, answers and notes drawn from a folder once the folder is purged. Any member may read. Change with organization-deleted-folder-content-set.

operations.name: organization-deleted-folder-content-set
operations.description: Chooses what happens to content derived from a folder when the folder is purged. Needs org:settings:manage. Takes effect at read time for all derived content at once. Read the current choice with organization-deleted-folder-content-get.

operations.name: organization-download-log-list
operations.description: Who took which document out, newest first, filtered by user, document, kind and day range (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD), paged by cursor (pass the cursor of the previous page). Needs org:downloads:view. Every read is recorded in the audit trail. Rows in folders the caller may not read come without document and folder names. User ids come from organization-member-list.

operations.name: organization-download-log-retention-set
operations.description: Sets how many whole days (30 to 365) the download log is kept. Needs org:settings:manage. A shorter time takes effect at the next daily purge, after which older entries cannot be recovered.

operations.name: organization-failed-document-reingest
operations.summary: Re-read every document that failed ingestion
operations.description: Queues a job that sends every document of the organization that could not be read back through ingestion, and answers at once with the job id. Needs org:settings:manage. For a single document use its own retry operation.

operations.name: organization-instructions-get
operations.description: The organization’s standing instruction block that shapes every answer its members get. Any member may read. Change it with organization-instructions-set.

operations.name: organization-instructions-set
operations.description: Replaces the organization’s standing instruction block with the given text; an empty or blank text clears it. Needs org:settings:manage. The block applies to every member’s answers, so read the current text with organization-instructions-get and edit it rather than overwriting it blindly.

operations.name: organization-member-list
operations.description: Every active member of the organization with user id, email and display name, read from the identity provider. Organization admins only. Use the user ids for per-member budgets (organization-budget-set) and for the userId filter of organization-download-log-list and organization-usage-get.

operations.name: organization-memory-create
operations.description: Records one item of organization-wide knowledge that every project then carries. Any member may add one. Returns the created item with its id. Check organization-memory-list first to avoid a duplicate.

operations.name: organization-memory-delete
operations.description: Permanently deletes one organization memory item; it cannot be undone. To keep it but stop using it, set its status with organization-memory-update instead. The id comes from organization-memory-list.

operations.name: organization-memory-list
operations.description: The knowledge shared by every project of the organization (kind, content, status, confidence, pinned). Any member may read. Item ids feed organization-memory-update and organization-memory-delete.

operations.name: organization-memory-update
operations.description: Changes fields of one organization memory item (kind, content, status, confidence, verification, pinned). At least one field is required. The id comes from organization-memory-list.

operations.name: organization-model-config-get
operations.description: The agent groups, the active model configuration version, whether zero data retention is on and applicable, and which groups have no ZDR-capable model. Needs org:models:manage. Pick models with organization-model-search, then save with organization-model-config-set.

operations.name: organization-model-config-set
operations.description: Validates the chosen model per agent group against the live catalog (and ZDR, while it is on), then writes a new version and activates it for the whole organization. Needs org:models:manage. Group ids come from organization-model-config-get, model ids from organization-model-search. The earlier version stays in organization-model-config-version-list for rollback.

operations.name: organization-model-config-version-activate
operations.summary: Roll back to a model configuration version
operations.description: Makes an earlier configuration version the active one for the whole organization, or pass the id "none" to drop every override and return to the inherited defaults. Needs org:models:manage. Refused with the offending groups when zero data retention is on and the version selects a model without a ZDR endpoint.

operations.name: organization-model-config-version-list
operations.description: The history of the organization’s model configurations, newest first, with the id of the active one. Needs org:models:manage. A version id goes to organization-model-config-version-activate to roll back.

operations.name: organization-model-search
operations.summary: Search models for an agent group
operations.description: Models that satisfy one agent group’s requirements, filtered by a search text, with context length, a ZDR mark and an approximate credit cost per request. Needs org:models:manage. The group id comes from organization-model-config-get; pass the chosen model id to organization-model-config-set.

operations.name: organization-role-list
operations.description: The roles of this organization (built-in and the office’s custom roles) by name and slug; any member may read them. Permissions and the list of assignable permissions are included only for holders of org:members:manage. Role slugs are what a folder restriction names.

operations.name: organization-settings-get
operations.description: Display name, default language and the settings bag of the caller’s organization. Any member may read. Change them with organization-settings-update.

operations.name: organization-settings-update
operations.description: Merges the provided fields into the organization’s settings: displayName, defaultLocale, and keys of the settings bag. Needs org:settings:manage. Keys that own a dedicated operation are refused: switch zero data retention with organization-zdr-set, the upload policy with organization-upload-screening-set, download log retention with organization-download-log-retention-set. Read the current values first with organization-settings-get.

operations.name: organization-storage-get
operations.description: How much storage the organization uses against its quota. Any member may read; the quota itself is set by the platform operator and cannot be changed here. Read this when an upload is refused.

operations.name: organization-upload-screening-get
operations.description: The policy that screens file names before an upload, whether it is still Piloti’s suggested list, and that suggestion. Any member may read. Change with organization-upload-screening-set.

operations.name: organization-upload-screening-set
operations.description: Replaces the organization’s upload screening policy. Needs org:settings:manage. Read the current policy and the suggested one with organization-upload-screening-get and send the whole policy.

operations.name: organization-usage-get
operations.description: Per-model usage by day and month in credits. Budget admins see the whole organization and may narrow it by userId or projectId; other members get their own usage only.

operations.name: organization-zdr-set
operations.summary: Turn zero data retention on or off
operations.description: Switches the organization’s zero-data-retention privacy control. On (the default) only models with a ZDR endpoint are accepted and every model request is sent with data collection denied; turning it off lets data reach endpoints that may retain it, so do it only when the person asks. Needs org:models:manage. The response names groups whose model has no ZDR endpoint; fix them with organization-model-config-set.
